beats.text: The team got a low stock alert for a product that was never low.
There were 120 in stock. The minimum is 100.
Then one order came in, for 10.
The save writes the row twice: first it releases everything, then it reserves what is left.
A trigger sees each write on its own, and asks one question: is it below the minimum?
The first write says zero, so it passes, and the alert goes out.
The second write says 110, and is turned back. Too late.
Over one day, that was six alerts. None of them was real.
The fix judges the whole save: where the row started, and where it ended.
Here is that order again, after the fix.
Going from 120 to 110 never crosses the line, so nothing is sent.
And when stock really drops to 90, the alert still goes out.
The cost: the trigger now has to hold every write until the save ends.
